Ray Hall and George Beecham were always well placed and provided the backing for team honours. John Keown walked well to complete our scoring four and was closely followed by D.

Ken Bailey walked magnificently in his first Brighton, George Beecham took third place after a steady race, and John Keown backed up well. Thanks must go to those who assisted our walkers, to mention just a few, Eric & Mavis Hall, Jack Goswell, Eric Beecham, and Don Bartliff.

Don Bartliff walked a good race with a well-sustained effort over the return journey. Ken Bailey seemed to be doing a steady training spin, while the extra miles suited Bernard Eglinton who shows steady improvement on each outing since his return from abroad.
Will Belderson recorded his best time ever (58:00) to finish 11th whilst Don Bartliff finished 20th in 59:05 and gained his 7 mile star for the first time.

Don Bartliff had taken over fourth team position for us, and confirmed that he has all the promise of championships to come in the years ahead; well backed by Ken Bailey, George Beecham, and Will Belderson.
The second handicap incorporated a match against M.P.A.A. which the Police won 33-45. Bob Barnes won the handicap from Don Bartliff and Ted Smith; Bob's time being 15:01.
With Bill Belderson and Don Bartliff following Mason home Belgrave won the team race by 3 points. Farley was the winner of the Belgrave handicap prize, put up by the home club.
Congratulations to Ray Hall on his captain's part of marshalling his team and to Bob Farley and Don Bartliff on their splendid efforts to snatch victory from the fire.
…ecs ahead of Edgington, with Nihill in 3rd place. Ray Hall did very well to finish 8th, followed by Bob Farley 10th and Don Bartliff, 17th.…

Ray Hall also walked well and by the finish had worked his way into 4th position, so the Bels had three men home before any other team finished one. With Bob Farley 11th, Don Bartliff 13th, and George Beecham 14th, our prospects for the London-Brighton in September look very bright.
Don Bartliff was 13th and completed the scoring team of three, but this was not quite good enough to beat S.W.C. who finished five men before our three.

At 10 miles this group were still together, and the Bels were very nicely placed for team points, but luck was not with us because Don Bartliff had to retire at this point with a hip injury when lying in 10th position.

Don Bartliff and Bill Belderson have both been posted elsewhere with the Police and we have seen little of them this year. Bob Barnes is now working in Cambridge and can only get down at weekends.
